chapter: The rhythm section, family and records
title: Refusing to leave Kansas City for New York without Walter Page
summary: Jones recalls the band insisting Page come to New York, begging his wife, and turning down higher-paying offers from Cab Calloway and Claude Hopkins.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: You mean the feeling that Walter Page instigated when he played?

You could not get it. I told you he was my father and he was my son. I was the last one to talk to him on the phone when we did the "Sound of Jazz". You was there... This man, this beautiful man, he had the capacity. Without him you never would have got us, because when we were leaving Kansas City to come to New York, his wife says, "No, he cannot go." We told Mr. Wilder Alexander, we told John Hammond, we told the man at the Roseland Ballroom - and the man is still alive and I will take you to him, offer this tape, and sit down and say, "Why did Basie's band come to New York?" We wasn't going to leave Walter Page in Kansas City. We begged his wife, "Let him come for a month and we'll send him back." We wasn't going to leave, Milt. We was making $17 a week
and $22 a week. We ain't leaving unless Walter Page go. Fess will tell you he tried to get three people out of the band at $75 a week -

- and $100 a week and Claude will tell you, because he had Buster Smith to join his band and he had to send Buster back at $100 a week. But we wasn't leaving Kansas City without Walter Page. We'd stay there till we rot. What will we do; we're poor little lambs lost?
He was definitely their leader, right, a leader of men and -

Bennie's dead! Who else are we going to look to? We don't know what to do! And Jack has got - Jack Washington's got to talk. His wife says no, he can't leave. This beautiful man, this father of us all, what do we know what to do? Basie don't....Don't nobody know what to do, until we go to Big'Un.
That's very beautiful, Joe. I think we ought to just knock this off and play a few of these very beautiful records and listen to a couple of records. I think it would do us a lot of good.
We got so wrapped up here and it was so beautiful, and this is the kind of thing we really want to capture...
This is the thing that I want you to get
in on, 'cause nobody'd do it. I told about this.
